questions.q: In the lab scenario, what triggers the creation of a new Problem record?
options: A third Incident reports the same VPN disconnect symptom, and no existing Problem record matches it
The first Incident reported is always escalated straight to a Problem
A user requests that a Problem be opened
ServiceNow automatically creates a Problem after any two Incidents with similar text
questions.explain: The agent working the third Incident checks for an existing Problem, finds none, and that recognized pattern is the trigger to open one.

questions.q: How do the three original Incidents get connected to the new Problem record?
options: Each Incident's `problem_id` field is set to point at the Problem record
Their short descriptions are manually rewritten to match the Problem's
They are merged into a single Incident record
They are closed and recreated as child Problems
questions.explain: Setting problem_id on each Incident is what populates the Problem's related list with all three linked tickets.

questions.q: In the scenario, why is the Problem flagged as a Known Error before the VPN concentrator setting is actually changed?
options: The root cause is confirmed, but the permanent fix requires a scheduled Change that hasn't happened yet
Known Error is flagged the instant any Problem record is created
A Known Error means the Problem is already fully resolved
Known Error only applies once all Incidents have been closed
questions.explain: Known Error is exactly this middle condition: cause confirmed, fix pending, often because it depends on a scheduled Change.

questions.q: Why can a fourth Incident, reported after the Known Error flag is set, be resolved quickly without re-investigation?
options: The documented workaround is now surfaced through search, so the agent applies it directly and links the Incident to the same Problem
The fourth Incident is automatically closed by the system with no agent action
The concentrator setting has already been permanently fixed by this point
The fourth Incident cannot be linked to the same Problem as the first three
questions.explain: This is the entire payoff of Known Error: the next agent gets the workaround fast instead of starting from zero.

questions.q: What finally moves the Problem from Known Error to Resolved in this scenario?
options: A scheduled Change adjusts the concentrator's session-timeout setting, and fix_notes records the permanent fix
A fifth Incident is reported with the same symptom
The workaround is simply used by enough users
Thirty days pass with no new Incidents
questions.explain: Resolution requires the permanent fix to actually be deployed and documented in fix_notes, not just a workaround in continued use.
